text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.revokeClaim / ClaimIssuer.revokeClaimBySignature / ClaimIssuer.getRecoveredAddress / ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid (used by IdentityRegistry.isVerified and Identity.addClaim)","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation is stored by the raw signature bytes, but signature verification normalizes v (v < 27 gets +27). A revoked signature with v=27 or 28 can be rewritten with v=0 or 1. The rewritten bytes are not in revokedClaims, yet they recover to the same signer, so the claim passes isClaimValid again. The investor wallet can re-add that claim, and isVerified then accepts the wallet, so a revoked wallet can receive tokens again.","steps":"1) Investor a1 holds a valid KYC claim (topic 1) from claimIssuer, stored in idA with signature S (v=27). 2) claimIssuer's admin calls claimIssuer.revokeClaim(claimId, idA), which sets revokedClaims[S]=true. 3) a1 calls idA.addClaim(1, 1, claimIssuer, S' , KYC_DATA, \"\") where S' is S with the last byte changed from 27 to 0. addClaim passes because isClaimValid normalizes v and the recovered signer is unchanged. S' is not in revokedClaims. 4) a1 (or a2 under idA) calls token.transfer(x, amount) to a verified receiver, and it succeeds, even though the KYC was revoked."}]}
